text: Confirm threshold logic: DiscountPolicy.discountRate() returns 0.10 when subtotalCents >= 10_000 for CustomerTier.REGULAR, else 0.0; PricingCalculator.calculateTotalCents rounds subtotal * (1 - discountRate).

In /src/test/java/com/sweforge/pricing/PricingCalculatorTest.java, add three @Test methods following the existing style (single Order built via List.of(new Item(...)), assertEquals(expected, calculator.calculateTotalCents(order))).
Case 1 (9,999 cents, below threshold): build an order whose items sum to 9,999 cents, e.g. new Item(9_999); expect no discount so expected total = 9,999.
Case 2 (10,000 cents, at threshold): build an order summing to 10,000 cents, e.g. new Item(10_000); expect 10% discount so expected total = 9,000.
Case 3 (10,001 cents, just above threshold): build an order summing to 10,001 cents, e.g. new Item(10_001); expect 10% discount so expected total = 9,001 (10_001 * 0.9 = 9000.9, rounds to 9001).
Name the new tests descriptively per existing convention, e.g. subtotalJustBelowThresholdHasNoDiscount, subtotalAtThresholdGetsBulkDiscount, subtotalJustAboveThresholdGetsBulkDiscount.
Do not modify DiscountPolicy.java, PricingCalculator.java, or any other production source file.
Run the relevant tests: mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test (Java 21) and confirm all cases pass, then optionally run the full mvn test per repository convention.
All three new tests pass, confirming 9,999 -> no discount, 10,000 and 10,001 -> 10% discount (rounded).
Existing tests (smallRegularOrderHasNoDiscount, largeRegularOrderGetsBulkDiscount, vipOrderGetsVipDiscount) still pass unmodified.
Diff shows changes only in PricingCalculatorTest.java; no production code files (DiscountPolicy.java, PricingCalculator.java, Item.java, Order.java, CustomerTier.java) are modified.
mvn test completes successfully for the whole module.
